# odinex_firewall (Resource)

Manages a firewall. Rules and targets (`apply_to`) are updated in place. Use either `apply_to` blocks or `odinex_firewall_attachment`, not both.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "odinex_firewall" "web" {
  name = "web"

  rule {
    direction  = "in"
    protocol   = "tcp"
    port       = "443"
    source_ips = ["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"]
  }

  apply_to {
    label_selector = "role=web"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the firewall.

### Optional

- `apply_to` (Block Set) Servers or label selectors the firewall applies to. Targets are only tracked while at least one `apply_to` block is configured (and are not imported); without blocks, targets managed by `odinex_firewall_attachment` are left alone. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--apply_to))
- `labels` (Map of String) User-defined labels (key/value pairs). Up to 64 pairs; keys and values up to 63 characters.
- `rule` (Block Set) A firewall rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique ID of the resource.

<a id="nestedblock--apply_to"></a>
### Nested Schema for `apply_to`

Optional:

- `label_selector` (String) Label selector, e.g. `role=web`.
- `server` (Number) ID of a server.


<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `direction` (String) `in` or `out`.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `esp` or `gre`.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Description of the rule.
- `destination_ips` (Set of String) Destination CIDRs; required for `out` rules.
- `port` (String) Port (`80`) or range (`1000-2000`); required for `tcp` and `udp`.
- `source_ips` (Set of String) Source CIDRs; required for `in` rules.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import odinex_firewall.web 5
```
